_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); oilfield services signals

pit_profile.why: Baker Hughes: 'Baker Hughes Incorporated is a Delaware corporation engaged in the oilfield services industry'; 'Within our oilfield operations, the primary driver of our businesses is our customers’ capital and operating expenditures dedicated to oil and natural gas exploration, field development and production'; 'Our business is cyclical and is dependent upon our customers’ expectations for future oil and natural gas prices, economic growth, hydrocarbon demand and estimates of current and future oil and natural gas production'; 'We operate in a highly competitive environment, which may adversely affect our ability to succeed'; 'In addition, demand for oil and natural gas could be impacted by environmental regulation, including “cap and trade” legislation, regulation of hydraulic fracturing, carbon taxes and the cost for carbon capture and sequestration related regulations' (its own FY2011 10-K): revenues and earnings that follow customers' drilling and production spending through the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; no disruption theme is live for an oilfield services company, so the greenhouse-gas wording stays here

classification.quality_note: Baker Hughes: 'Baker Hughes Incorporated is a Delaware corporation engaged in the oilfield services industry'; 'Within our oilfield operations, the primary driver of our businesses is our customers’ capital and operating expenditures dedicated to oil and natural gas exploration, field development and production'; 'Our business is cyclical and is dependent upon our customers’ expectations for future oil and natural gas prices, economic growth, hydrocarbon demand and estimates of current and future oil and natural gas production'; 'We operate in a highly competitive environment, which may adversely affect our ability to succeed'; 'In addition, demand for oil and natural gas could be impacted by environmental regulation, including “cap and trade” legislation, regulation of hydraulic fracturing, carbon taxes and the cost for carbon capture and sequestration related regulations' (its own FY2011 10-K): revenues and earnings that follow customers' drilling and production spending through the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; no disruption theme is live for an oilfield services company, so the greenhouse-gas wording stays here. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price fair; Ratio B 0.91x; +0% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.06; conservative 2yr +23%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -74.3%/yr (worst year FY02-FY12, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +-4.0%/yr (Q4 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +12.3%/yr (FY02-FY12 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +74.5%/yr (best 2-yr run FY02-FY12); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: BHI (retrospective, 2013-02-01) ◎ ACCUMULATE — Ratio B 0.91x (93.3% downside to Bear $3 / +102.1% upside to Bull $91) | Adj composite 2.00 vs market 2.06: gap -0.06 [FAIRLY VALUED] | +0% above the EPP floor $45 (15x FY13E $3.00) | Conservative 2-yr case: +22.7% total (+11.3%/yr) | At 15.0x FY13E the 15% hurdle price $60 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; North America revenue -9.5% and revenue outside North America +8.6% in Q4 2012, forward revenues -1.4% (no Q1 2013 revenue guide, Q4 2012 revenue as reported); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
